findings.current:
“May I order some alcohol? I’ve never had any before.”

“…”

This kid had a lot of things he had never tried.
findings.defect: Taekyung’s spoken permission to order alcohol is omitted and replaced by silence, changing his response and weakening the setup for Cheongpung choosing the cheapest bottle.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly has Taekyung pause and then grant permission; the ellipsis is not his entire response.
findings.replacement:
“May I order some alcohol? I’ve never had any before.”

“…Order as much as you like.”

This kid had a lot of things he had never tried.
findings.source:
“술 좀 시켜도 될까요? 제가 아직 술을 못 먹어 봐서.”

“……얼마든지 시키세요.”

findings.defect: The draft drops Taekyung’s comic self-correction from “a little” to “very,” an intentional pragmatic shift prompted by Cheongpung’s voracious eating.
findings.rationale: 좀…… 많이 deliberately changes the degree mid-sentence rather than merely pausing before a single description.
findings.replacement: “You must’ve been a little… very hungry.”

findings.current: My grandfather lived alone in the mountains his entire life, too.
findings.defect: The simple past can imply that Cheongpung’s grandfather is dead or no longer lives there, although the following conversation establishes that he is alive and still moving between residences.
findings.rationale: The grandfather is subsequently described in the present tense as continuing to avoid visitors, so the English should preserve the continuing state.
findings.replacement: My grandfather has lived alone in the mountains his entire life, too.
findings.source: 저희 할아버지도 산에서 평생 혼자 사셨는걸요.

findings.current:
“Plum Pork.”

“Plum Pork?”

I knew Megumi, who lived in the island country next door, but this was my first time hearing of Plum Pork. The waiter answered irritably, as though I had inconvenienced him.

“Preserved Vegetable Pork.”

“…”

Now he was shortening the names, too.

While I stood there dumbfounded, Cheongpung was rapidly emptying the plates.
findings.defect: Translating 매구 as “Plum Pork” destroys the sound-based Megumi joke and no longer reads as a recognizable abbreviation of the expanded dish name. The passage also adds that seated Taekyung “stood there,” an action absent from the source.
findings.rationale: The humor depends mechanically on 매구 being both an abbreviation of 매채구육 and phonetically close to 메구미; the localized dish names preserve neither relationship.
findings.replacement:
“Maegu.”

“Maegu?”

I’d heard of Megumi from the island country next door, but Maegu was a new one to me. Catching my look, the waiter answered as if explaining it was a chore.

“Maechae Guyuk.”[^2]

“…”

Now he was even abbreviating dish names.

While I stared at him in disbelief, Cheongpung rapidly emptied the plates.

[^2]: *Maechae Guyuk* is pork belly with preserved mustard greens. The waiter shortens its Korean name to *Maegu*, which sounds like the beginning of the Japanese name Megumi.
findings.source:
“매구.”

“매구?”

옆 동네 섬나라 사는 메구미는 알아도 매구는 처음 들어 본다. 내 시선에 점소이가 귀찮다는 듯이 대답했다.

“매채구육(梅采拘肉)이요.”

“…….”

이제는 하다 하다 줄임말까지 쓰는구나.

내가 어이없어하는 사이 청풍은 빠르게 음식 접시를 비워 나가고 있었다.

findings.current:
“Is it against the law not to know?”

“Of course it is. The Second Young Master is one of them, after all.”
findings.defect: The draft invents a law-based joke absent from the source and makes Mujin affirm that knowing the term is literally required by law.
findings.rationale: The Korean exchange is a blunt argument over whether Taekyung is allowed not to know, without any reference to legality.
findings.replacement:
“Can’t I just not know?”

“Of course you can’t. The Second Young Master is one of them, after all.”
findings.source:
“모르면 안 되냐?”

“당연히 안 되죠. 당장 이공자님이 십봉룡인데.”

findings.current: “Everything was my first time eating it, so I made a spectacle of myself in front of my Benefactors. I hope I wasn’t too excessive…”
findings.defect: “Everything was my first time eating it” is ungrammatical and “too excessive” is an unnatural collocation.
findings.rationale: The replacement naturally conveys that every dish was new to Cheongpung and preserves his polite concern that he behaved immoderately.
findings.replacement: “It was my first time trying any of these dishes, so I made a spectacle of myself in front of my Benefactors. I hope I didn’t overdo it…”
findings.source: “다 처음 먹어 보는 음식이라 은인들 앞에서 추태를 보였습니다. 제가 너무 과하진 않았는지…….”

findings.current: “If it wouldn’t be too much trouble, may I have just one candied hawthorn skewer?”
findings.defect: The required first-use explanatory footnote for 빙당호로 is missing.
findings.rationale: The binding terminology explicitly requires candied hawthorn skewers to receive an explanatory footnote.
findings.replacement:
“If it wouldn’t be too much trouble, may I have just one candied hawthorn skewer?[^1]”

[^1]: Candied hawthorn skewers are a traditional Chinese snack made by coating skewered fruit in hardened sugar.
findings.source: “실례가 안 된다면 빙당호로 하나만 먹어도 되겠습니까?”

summary: Two major fidelity issues and five localized omissions or wording problems are actionable.
